**Finding: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data)**

**What I found**
- §2(d) (p0029) is the only ownership provision and runs one way — TrueLink retains all ownership in the Interface (fine in itself; vendor platform ownership is acceptable).
- There is no counterpart clause confirming that Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, Credit Data or other Client data remain ours, and nothing addresses ownership of, or a perpetual licence to, the Support Services results we pay for under §4.
- §10 (p0063, p0065) only makes Client's Intellectual Property and "all results of the Hosting and Support Services" confidential — a secrecy obligation, not ownership or a licence.
- §13 (p0078) says we retain ownership of domains and Client Content, but only in the discontinued-service context.
- §8(d) (p0054) licenses narrowly defined, aged Credit Data to TrueLink on a non-exclusive basis subject to the Non-Competition Agreement — a licence, not an assignment, so I did not flag it as walk-away.

Neither the preferred nor the fallback position is met on a material term (no Customer Data ownership statement; no ownership of or perpetual, irrevocable licence to work product), so a redline is warranted.

**Proposed redline (validated, ok:true)** — new §2(e) inserted after p0029 reserving our content, IP and data, assigning Support Services work product to us, licensing back any embedded TrueLink IP on a perpetual, royalty-free basis, and excluding joint ownership. Comment offers the fallback (TrueLink keeps generic tools/know-how provided we keep the perpetual licence).
